title: Annif at SemEval-2025 Task 5: Traditional XMTC augmented by LLMs
venue: Proceedings of the 19th International Workshop on Semantic Evaluation (SemEval-2025)
extended_summary:
This paper does not report on the targeted education study titled "The role of AI assisted writing feedback in developing secondary students writing skills." Instead, it describes a SemEval-2025 shared task system for automated subject indexing of bibliographic records. The paper addresses the problem of assigning subject labels from the German National Library’s GND vocabulary to multilingual records from the TIBKAT database, framing the task as extreme multilabel text classification in library and information science rather than an educational intervention study.

The authors’ approach combines the Annif subject indexing toolkit with several machine learning backends—Omikuji Bonsai, MLLM, and XTransformer—and augments these traditional methods with large language models for preprocessing. Specifically, LLMs were used to translate bibliographic records into monolingual German and English versions, translate subject vocabulary terms, and generate synthetic training records. The resulting systems were combined in ensembles and evaluated in SemEval-2025 Task 5, where the best configuration ranked first in the all-subjects category and second in the tib-core-subjects category in quantitative evaluation.

The population and context are bibliographic database records from the TIBKAT catalog and subject librarians conducting qualitative evaluation, not students or teachers in schools. There is no secondary-school writing population, no AI writing feedback intervention in classrooms, and no measurement of student writing skill development. The study context is multilingual automated indexing infrastructure for library metadata, with technical experimentation conducted by researchers at the National Library of Finland and the University of Helsinki.

The strongest evidence-based resolution is that the provided paper is a retrieval mismatch and not the requested secondary education study. Based on the text supplied, the target study was not found here; this record appears to have been conflated with an unrelated 2025 AI paper because both involve LLMs. Therefore, no valid extraction about AI-assisted writing feedback for secondary students can be made from this text, and the requested study is best treated as not located in the provided evidence.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a SemEval shared-task system description on automated subject indexing for bibliographic records, not an education intervention study. It reports benchmark/task performance but provides no student-facing educational intervention, no K-12 sample, and no causal or correlational educational evaluation methodology.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper shows competitive technical performance for multilingual library subject indexing, but it does not measure effects on student learning, teacher practice, or institutional education outcomes. Educational impact is therefore unclear and not directly evidenced.
